  *   *   *   *   * ## Clinical Trials for Veterinary Imaging

### Canine Cancer Clinical Trial

This clinical trial will enroll a total of 5-7 dogs in order to confirm that ^{18}F DCFPyl PET-CT offers an improved sensitivity for the early detection of hemangiosarcoma cancer or metastatic prostate cancer.

### Canine Metastatic Cancer Clinical Trial

This clinical trial will enroll 5-10 dogs to evaluate the efficacy of a novel chemotherapeutic agent called IF7-SN38. This trial includes dogs with metastatic disease. This chemotherapy is delivered intravenously as a series, every other day for three to five days.

### Canine Brain Cancer Clinical Trial

This clinical trial will enroll 5-10 dogs to evaluate the efficacy of a novel chemotherapeutic agent called IF7-SN38. This chemotherapy is delivered intravenously as a series, every other day for three to five days.

# UC Davis Veterinary Medicine Recruiting Dogs for Glioma Clinical Trials

UC Davis Weill School of Veterinary Medicine

11,012 followers

5d

The UC Davis Weill School of Veterinary Medicine is recruiting dogs with suspected or confirmed glioma for two clinical trials exploring new approaches to diagnosis, treatment, and disease monitoring. The CARE Trial is investigating an experimental drug in combination with radiation therapy. The PRISM Trial offers radiation therapy and observational/palliative pathways while studying the relationship between clinical signs, disease progression and tumor biology. Together, these studies aim to improve our understanding of canine glioma and its molecular characteristics, with potential implications for both veterinary and human medicine. 🔗 Learn more and see if your dog may be eligible: https://lnkd.in/gdn2AuNF Financial support is available toward eligible diagnostic and treatment costs, and participating dogs are monitored by the UC Davis veterinary neuro-oncology team. Participation does not guarantee an improved outcome. Eligibility is determined by the clinical trial team. #VeterinaryClinicalTrials | #CanineCancer | #Glioma Image description: A dog enrolled in a UC Davis clinical trial for canine glioma alongside members of the veterinary research team. # Pet Trial Finder Launches to Simplify Clinical Trial Recruitment

Brycen Levings

4mo

Today, we’re proud to officially launch Pet Trial Finder. After three months of focused development and an additional three months of beta testing with veterinary partners, we are excited to bring this platform to market. Pet Trial Finder was co-founded by Tariq Shah and myself to address a critical challenge in veterinary oncology: clinical trial recruitment and accessibility. Too often, eligible patients are unaware of appropriate studies, and clinics lack streamlined tools to efficiently match cases to trials. Our platform simplifies this process. By collecting key details about a pet’s diagnosis and medical history, Pet Trial Finder identifies relevant clinical trials and connects owners and referring veterinarians directly with study coordinators to evaluate eligibility and next steps. Clinical trials not only advance veterinary medicine and oncology research — they can also provide access to innovative therapies at reduced or no cost, potentially saving pet owners thousands of dollars while contributing to scientific progress. We’re excited to support veterinary teams, researchers, and pet families in accelerating access to cutting-edge treatment options. If you’re involved in veterinary oncology research or interested in partnering, we’d love to connect.

# Enzistat Veterinary Clinical Trial Launches at University of Queensland

Aditya Kulkarni

4mo Edited

A Global First for Veterinary Oncology! We are proud to announce the launch of the Enzistat veterinary (canine) clinical trial at The University of Queensland led by Prof. Rachel Allavena and Dr. José Granados Soler. This trial represents a series of "firsts" that push the boundaries of how we treat our companions animals. World’s First: The first-ever veterinary clinical trial for an oral immunooncology drug. We are moving away from complex infusions toward accessible, "off-the-shelf" oral immune modulating treatments for canine cancer. A "Make in India" Milestone: Enzistat is likely the first-ever veterinary oncology drug developed wholly in India to reach this stage of clinical validation. # Purdue Vet Launches Canine Cancer Immunotherapy Trial

Purdue University College of Veterinary Medicine & Veterinary Hospital

8,630 followers

8mo

Purdue Veterinary Medicine Announces Enrollment for a New Canine Cancer Immunotherapy Trial The Purdue University Veterinary Hospital Oncology Service is launching a clinical trial evaluating an innovative PD-L1 immunotherapy vaccine for dogs. This approach, modeled after transformative immune-checkpoint therapies in human oncology, works by blocking PD-L1 and restoring the immune system’s ability to recognize and target cancer cells. Study benefits for enrolled dogs: • Three vaccine doses across six weeks • No placebo groups • Close clinical monitoring by Purdue’s oncology team • Access to a therapy designed specifically for canine patients Eligible cancer types: T-zone lymphoma, melanoma, osteosarcoma, mast cell tumor, soft tissue sarcoma, squamous cell carcinoma, mammary carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma. Enrollment criteria: Dogs must be over 1 year old, over 18 lbs, have biopsy-accessible tumors, be able to undergo sedation, and not have received recent chemo, steroids, radiation, or targeted therapy.

# Veterinarians Lack Unified Study Recruitment Platform

Evan Nison

1mo Edited

Yesterday I took my dog to his preventive oncologist (yes, he has one). While I was there I asked the doctor a simple question: "Is there any tool or website that should exist for your profession but doesn't?" Without hesitation he told me that there's no single place where veterinarians can find all active veterinary studies that are currently recruiting participants. Right now, vets have to go to each university's website individually to check. That's a massive time sink and it means eligible patients are getting missed. Less than 24 hours later, it's built. This is the use case for AI that I get most excited about. Listening to important professionals describe a gap in their workflow and closing it before the week is out. ### Drug Targeting Program

Innovation in drug delivery

Image: Picture2.png

The other research program of Dr. Komatsu's laboratory is to develop and examine novel vascular targeting strategies for target-specific drug delivery guided by specific peptides. Peptide-directed vascular targeting takes advantage of unique molecular signatures of blood vessels at specific locations in the body

Originally developed by Dr. Erkki Ruoslahti, this technology enables the direct delivery of drugs to tumors or other diseased tissues through the vascular network. 

Since drugs are targeted to specific disease sites, it is possible to enhance drug efficacy while reducing the effective dose and minimizing adverse effects associated with standard chemotherapies. In collaboration with IF7Cure, Dr. Komatsu has been advancing the clinical development of IF7-SN38, an IF7 peptide-conjugated chemotherapeutic agent. IF7-SN38  
Cancer Trial in Dogs

To assess the effectiveness of a novel chemotherapeutic in dogs with cancer.

Baseline screening performed at your veterinarian is required for entrance into the study.

Inclusion Criteria
- Dog is a minimum of nine months of age;
- Dog has no major concurrent health issue;
- Dog is eligible to begin chemotherapy immediately;
- Dog has been diagnosed with cancer and the largest tumor < 3cm;
- Dogs with metastatic disease and/or resistant to standard of care therapy will be considered;
- Pet owner is willing and able to sign a consent form and comply with all study procedures for the duration of the study

Exclusion Criteria
- Anticipated life expectancy < 3 weeks;
- Single or double positive for MDR1 genetic mutation;
- Evidence of serious systemic disorder;
- Any condition that may preclude the evaluation of safety and/or activity of the study drug;
- Other concurrent cancer treatment, investigational drug or intervention
